body:
It might be getting late early for Mike Boynton, and Elliot Cadeau's lack of impact as the veteran point guard is a big issue
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 26, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:12 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        LAS VEGAS — A year ago, Michigan won the Players Era Tournament by putting up a historic 110-point margin of victory across three games. It was a harbinger for its 37-3 NCAA championship season.Through two games this year at the Players Era 16, everything has flipped to the dark side. The Wolverines are 0-2 in Sin City and -53 in scoring margin after losing to Creighton on Tuesday and Miami on Thursday, giving up 196 points in the process. Michigan got dropped 97-70 by the No. 17 Hurricanes on Thanksgiving, two days after Creighton crushed the Wolverines 99-73.Michigan has already lost more games by Thanksgiving than it did all of last season.Mike Boynton's team is 3-4, which doubles as the worst start through seven games for a reigning national champion since Louisville in 1986, meaning it's been four decades since college basketball's seen an encore this dubious from a program fresh off a March Madness title.
All four of Michigan's losses have come at neutral-site contests; the Wolverines were 11-2 in those settings last season. November's nearly finished and Boynton's only notable win came at home on Nov. 11 against a 4-3 Marquette team that is just as TBD in quality as Michigan right now."Our defense just went completely away (in the second half)," Boynton said outside the locker room of T-Mobile Arena after the loss to Miami. "There's no excuses. We got our butt kicked today."Boynton already in a big bindAs Dusty May tours through his debut NBA season with the Dallas Mavericks, Boynton finds himself in charge of the program May flipped in record-setting fashion after things bottomed out under the controversial Juwan Howard era. It's too soon to definitively call this Michigan team a bust, but initial indications are not encouraging. Keep in mind, Boynton was promoted in-house due to the awkward timing of May leaving the program during the week of the NBA Draft. Outgoing Michigan athletic director Warde Manuel made a few cursory check-ins, but no sitting high-major coach was going to leave for a Michigan roster that would've lost at least three or four players if Boynton wasn't promoted.
Granted, Michigan lost not just a great coach, but three lottery picks (Yaxel Lendeborg, Aday Mara, Morez Johnson) who comprised the best frontcourt in college basketball last season. A step back was unavoidable and to be expected.This is no step-back, though. Michigan's in the midst of a plunge. A sub-.500 start through seven games is just as bad as what the football team's gone through in Kyle Whittingham's first (and maybe last?) season in Ann Arbor. In fact, Boynton's fortunate that this Vegas crap-out has come during the week of The Game in football and amid the PR disaster of the school's botched athletic director search.Michigan's coaching staff will feel the disappointment and pressure all the same, however. The Wolverines don't even look good enough to qualify for 76-team NCAA Tournament. Michigan ranked No. 1 in defensive efficiency a year ago. Through Thanksgiving, the Wolverines are 119th in adjusted defensive efficiency at BartTorvik.com. Every doubter who said Boynton should not have been given the job is justified in the here and now. 
Michigan coach Mike Boynton tries to motivate the Wolverines before Thursday's loss to Miami. 
                                                                    Getty Images
                                                            "As a coach, I've got to address it and find a way to fix it," Boynton said. "And maybe this team's defensive identity needs to be different than what we expected coming into the season."After a generous benefit of the doubt from the media going into November (Michigan was ranked 16th in the first AP Top 25), the Wolverines have fallen outside of the top 50 in every mainstream predictive metric after the Miami mauling on Thursday. Things might be different if the Wolverines had five-star freshman prospect Brandon McCoy, but he's out for the year with a torn ACL (and will likely be a top-25 pick next year without ever having played a game in college)."This team obviously has had the expectations of who they would be reset in a major way," Boynton said. "It's November, but November is also almost over, and right now we're staring at being under .500. And, like, you don't get a whole lot of chances to waste, even though you're playing in a conference as good as ours, you've got to start turning these things into Ws pretty quick."
Not helping the cause: fifth-year wing Roddy Gayle left Thursday's game with an injury and was seen on crutches leaving the arena. But Boynton told CBS Sports that the hope is the injury isn't serious and long-term in nature. An update probably won't come for Gayle until Friday.Cadeau goes from MOP to MIA  One of U-M's biggest, most obvious complications is the lack of consistency from senior point guard Elliot Cadeau, who won the Final Four Most Outstanding Player award less than eight months ago. Through Michigan's first seven games he doesn't look like one of the 40 best point guards in America. On Thursday against Miami, Cadeau had 15 points on 20 shots, including 1-of-9 3-point shooting, in addition to eight assists, five turnovers and four fouls. He's shooting less than 35% this season and has a sub-90 offensive rating at KenPom. His averages include 11.3 points and 4.3 turnovers. You can't be a good team, let alone really good, when your veteran point guard isn't playing up to his end of the bargain. And when Boynton was asked postgame about what players are stepping up and displaying leadership amid this terrible start, he didn't invoke Cadeau's name.
"I think we're still trying to figure that out," he said. "The best teams are going to have that voice internally from somebody or a couple (of) guys, and right now we're just still searching for it."That shouldn't be the case, not with someone like Cadeau who has 115 college starts.Cadeau is a senior, one of the most well-compensated veteran guards in the sport and a crucial part of this team. With him running the offense, Michigan ranks 202nd in turnover percentage and is giving the ball away on 18% of its possessions. Last season's team had a TO bugaboo as well, but it was offset by ridiculous size, paint-smothering second-chance opportunities and switchable bigs who made life a whole lot easier for Cadeau.

        
            
                Duke beat UConn, which was big. John Blackwell's night was even bigger — and so crucial for Duke's title hopes
                
                    Matt Norlander                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
"We have guys capable, certainly, because we have several guys who've been through these battles at this level who understand what it looks like to turn the page, to deal with adversity," Boynton said. "But that's got to evolve. Those voices have to emerge, and again, until then it's on me and the staff to be the voice and try to get these guys to understand how to deal with the challenges that we're facing right now."Michigan's last game in Vegas will be Friday afternoon against the loser of Thursday's Alabama vs. Kansas State game. You best believe the staff is hoping it's K-State; you can bet that with more confidence than any table game or slot machine on the Strip. The Wolverines need a win to halt the negative results and to get out of November at .500. Then December will arrive and they can try to pick up the pieces and see if it's possible to swing back into the top third of the Big Ten. The afterglow of an all-time-dominant NCAA title run is officially over and Boynton's job will soon hang in the balance, if it's not already.

John Calipari's Razorbacks face Tom Izzo's Spartans in a marquee nonconference matchup in Detroit in the CBS Sports Thanksgiving Classic

        For the third consecutive year, Arkansas will be making an appearance in the CBS Sports Thanksgiving Classic. The Razorbacks have a showdown on Thursday in Detroit against No. 11 Michigan State in a marquee nonconference showdown. Arkansas faced Illinois on Thanksgiving in 2024 and played Duke last season on CBS.This game will be played in the same city as this season's Final Four site. Michigan State and Arkansas will play at Little Caesars Arena, home of the Detroit Pistons. Not far down the road is Ford Field, the site of the 2027 Final Four. Both teams hope this won't be their last trip to Detroit this season.Arkansas is off to a 4-2 start in John Calipari's third season at the helm of the program. The Razorbacks are 0-2 against high-major opponents, with losses coming against No. 2 Virginia and No. 23 Indiana. Since taking over at Arkansas, Calipari is 6-12 against AP top 15 teams.Meanwhile, Michigan State improved to 5-1 after defeating Detroit Mercy last week. Before that game, MSU suffered its first loss of the season against Tennessee on the road. Michigan State is 1-1 against high-major teams, with the win coming against Duke in the Champions Classic.
Where to watch Michigan State vs. Arkansas liveDate: Thursday, Nov. 26 | Time: 4:30 p.m. ETLocation: Little Caesars Arena -- DetroitTV: CBS | Live stream: CBSSports.com, CBS Sports App Streaming on Paramount+ Premium
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Michigan State vs. Arkansas: Need to knowLegendary coaches meet again: This game will feature two of college basketball's greatest coaches: Tom Izzo and Calipari. Calipari and Izzo have the same number of NCAA Tournament wins (61), Sweet 16 appearances (17), and national titles (1). Calipari has the fourth-most wins by a Division I coach (909), while MSU has reached the NCAA Tournament 28 consecutive seasons under Izzo.This game could be a turning point for Arkansas: Entering the season, there was bound to be growing pains for Arkansas. That's because the Razorbacks returned just one player (Billy Richmond III) from their rotation last season. Arkansas loaded up in high school recruiting, which was headlined by the signing of five-star Jordan Smith Jr. One player from that class who has impressed recently is Davion Thompson. The former four-star scored a season-high 20 points against Indiana last week. Calipari's team may need some time to mesh, but this is still one of the most talented rosters in college basketball.
Jeremy Fears Jr. continues his player of the year campaign: Fears is off to an incredible start to the season and will be firmly in the mix to win the sport's top individual honor. Although he struggled against Tennessee (didn't make a field goal in that game), he bounced back with a double-double (17 points and 14 assists) against Detroit Mercy. Fears is currently leading the nation in assists per game (9.3) this season. He finished first in that stat among all Division I players last season.Michigan State vs. Arkansas prediction, pickMichigan State couldn't buy a bucket against Tennessee and struggled out of the gate against Detroit Mercy before pulling away in the second half. Meanwhile, Arkansas nearly beat Indiana. Something is going to have to give in this game. The key stat to watch is Michigan State's offensive rebounding. The Spartans are elite at creating second chances and getting to the free-throw line. If Arkansas can limit those second chances, they will have a chance to limit the possessions. I'll take Arkansas to cover, although I think Michigan State will win this game if they can make a double-digit amount of field goals, something they couldn't do during a loss vs. Tennessee. Pick: Arkansas +5.5

body:
The rivalry between USC and UCLA took an odd turn off the field
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 26, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:13 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        The rivalry between USC and UCLA is already heated enough on the field, but it doesn't always stay within the lines. The USC band pranked the Bruins this week, and now it will pay the price.This week, members of the Trojan Marching Band tampered with the sign on the Wasserman Football Center, turning it into "Ass Football Center." Photos of the prank went viral, and USC president Beong-Soo Kim stepped in to discipline the entire band.In a statement released on Wednesday night, Kim apologized to UCLA and announced his decision to bar the USC band from performing at the Rose Bowl this weekend.
"Out of respect for UCLA, and to provide time to reflect on the collective responsibility we share to uphold our university's values, the university and the Trojan Marching Band's leadership have decided that the band will not take the field for their traditional pre-game and halftime performances at the Rose Bowl on Saturday," Kim said in a statement.
Perhaps this prank highlights just how important the game is to both sides this season. It's the first time since 2005 that the Trojans (8-3) and Bruins (10-1) are ranked inside the top 25. Both are also still alive for a spot in the Big Ten Championship Game, and UCLA is clinging to a spot in the College Football Playoff.
The Bruins will be looking for revenge on Saturday — both because of this prank and as they look to end a two-game losing streak to their cross-town rival. This top-15 matchup kicks off at 3:30 p.m.  ET on Saturday, and you can catch all the action on CBS and Paramount+ Premium.

        The College Football Playoff Selection Committee put the sport on notice with the release of its rankings on Tuesday evening. Almost no one is safe heading into the final week of the season, and the bubble is still wide open. Specifically, the Big 12 and Big Ten are jockeying for position in the final weeks. The Big 12 projects to have three teams in the field if they can take care of business. The Big Ten has the first four teams out of the field. Resumes are still being built and can quickly crumble under stress. With that in mind, here are five games that could have a major impact on the College Football Playoff race in the final days of the regular season. No. 9 UCLA vs. No. 15 USCThe Bruins are perhaps the most precarious team in the entire College Football Playoff picture. Heading into last week, UCLA was undefeated and a surefire bye candidate from the Big Ten. After falling to Michigan and losing quarterback Ty Dieffenbach for at least some period of time, that could quickly change. 
USC has been inconsistent this season, but the Trojans are one of the most talented teams in the Big Ten. They're heavy favorites for this matchup at the Rose Bowl. A second loss for UCLA almost certainly pushes them out of the playoff. Can they find a way? 
        
            
                Tracking FBS conference championship scenarios: Big Ten, SEC still unsettled entering Week 13
                
                    Austin Nivison                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
No. 6 Alabama vs. AuburnThe Iron Bowl always has stakes unto itself, but the Crimson Tide need a strong finish to the season after their resume has fallen by the wayside. Alabama has not won this season against a team with more than seven wins, and their last victory against a four-loss team or better was in September. Auburn pulled an upset against No. 1 Georgia earlier this season, so the upside and playmaking are there. If the Crimson Tide can't perform against Auburn, it could make the committee seriously consider the strength of their resume. Spoiler: It's not great. 
No. 11 Texas Tech vs. TCUTCU has quietly been one of the best defenses in the Big 12, dragging Utah and BYU underwater for a half each. Texas Tech was held to only 20 points against Baylor last week, and this could be the toughest test of the season so far since switching to Thomas Castellanos. With a win, the Red Raiders can clinch a spot in the Big 12 Championship Game for the second straight season. A loss would almost certainly push them out of playoff consideration. The stakes are high in Lubbock. No. 3 Texas vs. Texas A&MTexas is unlikely to fall out of the playoff race, even with a loss to a horrendous Texas A&M team, but the Aggies could complicate their lives. A loss would push the Longhorns into the morass of three-loss teams, potentially taking them from a first-round bye to the risk of a first-round road game -- and even playing Georgia in the second round. Texas would benefit greatly from winning. 
No. 10 BYU vs. CincinnatiThe Cougars are no longer in control of their path for the Big 12 Championship, meaning that they need some help from the College Football Playoff committee to get into the field. Of course, BYU has also been perhaps the most disrespected team by the CFP over the past two years, never making the postseason despite a combined 23-4 record. Against Cincinnati, BYU's offense must rise to the occasion. The Cougars are a machine at LaVell Edwards Stadium. But after heading into triple overtime against Kansas, BYU needs to lay on the style points to leave a positive impression on the committee. No. 12 Oregon vs. No. 24 WashingtonWho would have thought that 4-3 Oregon would have a serious shot to get back into the College Football Playoff picture? If there's even a single upset in the top 10, the Ducks are now the first team that would benefit. 
However, they must get past a Washington team that has quietly been playing better football, winning four of their last five games. A win would launch the Huskies to a promising 8-4 season with several players poised to return. It's a tone-setting game for the Ducks. UTSA vs. TulsaWith Boise State's loss against San Diego State last week, the Group of Six race finds itself in a dead heat. The Broncos are still projected as the G6 rep, but the Roadrunners are slowly but surely making a case. The Roadrunners sit at 9-2 and 6-1 in American play, holding sole possession of first place in the conference. They finish the year at the Alamodome against Tulsa, a promising upstart that would love nothing better than clinching its first eight-win season since 2016. 
With rumors swirling around coach Jeff Traylor's name in the coaching carousel, can UTSA block out the noise?

body:
Former Packers players criticized Rodgers for attacking McCarthy publicly and putting his ex-Steelers teammates in an uncomfortable position

        Aaron Rodgers' recent comments about Mike McCarthy have drawn the ire of some of his former Green Bay Packers teammates. Former Packers offensive lineman T.J. Lang and former Packers receivers James Jones and Greg Jennings have publicly denounced Rodgers' treatment of McCarthy while taking their former coach's side following a chaotic 48-hour period in Pittsburgh. Rodgers scorched McCarthy on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday, accusing his now-former coach of falling asleep at meetings, being late or absent from other meetings, not watching film in a timely manner and not developing a rapport with some of his players, especially the team's defensive players. Rodgers was benched after giving McCarthy an ultimatum: relinquish play-calling duties or release him. McCarthy benched Rodgers, and the Steelers released him after Rodgers publicly criticized McCarthy. "I think it's despicable," Lang said on 97.1 The Ticket in Detroit. "I think that Aaron Rodgers just became everything that he has bitched about and moaned about over the last 10 years with former coaches, former teammates airing grievances out, giving opinions out in the media. He has blacklisted, I don't know how many former teammates from just simple comments telling the truth because he just he was sick of it."Lang, who spent eight seasons with Rodgers and McCarthy in Green Bay, said that he is in a group chat with several former Packers who share his sentiment on the situation. 
"I think it's just completely unnecessary," he said. "I think it's victim mentality." 
Jones, who also spent eight seasons with Rodgers and McCarthy in Green Bay, said he, too, is in a group text with former Packers teammates who don't agree with Rodgers' handling of McCarthy. "How do you jump on Pat McAfee's show and say all this? Come on, man," Jones said on the Speakeasy podcast. "My text thread is full of texts and group chats with a lot of my teammates right now, and none are on 12's side, especially the ones that know Mike."  
Jennings, who spent seven seasons in Green Bay and caught two touchdowns in the Packers' Super Bowl win over the Steelers, called Rodgers' decision to publicly air his grievances with McCarthy "distasteful." Jennings also criticized Rodgers for putting his former teammates in Pittsburgh in an awkward situation. "If you truly cared about more than just yourself, then you don't do this to everybody in that locker room that you just called brothers," Jennings said on "First Thing First." "They are playing for something. You are no longer playing for anything." 
The general consensus among Rodgers' former Packers teammates is that Rodgers should have handled the situation behind closed doors, even if some of his accusations about McCarthy are true. 
"I don't even care if it's the truth," Jones said. "Have the conversation with Mike in there. This is not something you go to the media bashing somebody. I would not do this to people that I love."

Welcome to the most special week in the NFL. We watched the Los Angeles Rams defeat the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night, and now, we have three exciting Thanksgiving matchups to digest this "Turkey Day."Football fans suffered through many sleepy Chicago Bears vs. Detroit Lions Thanksgiving matchups over the years. Now, this 1 p.m. game on Thursday is expected to be one of the most exciting holiday matchups in recent memory. After that, the Dallas Cowboys will welcome Joe Milton III and the Philadelphia Eagles to AT&T Stadium. Both teams are coming off wins, and the Cowboys need this game if they want to keep pace in the NFC East. At the end of the night, we have a potential AFC Championship preview to watch when the Buffalo Bills host Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs. This is just the second game in NFL history to feature two teams coming off at least three straight 17-point victories. Which teams should you pick in Week 12, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 25 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports ResearchDenver Broncos (-3.5) at Pittsburgh Steelers (Friday)Dajani (Broncos -3.5): Aaron Rodgers lobbed a grenade into the Pittsburgh Steelers facility as he exited it this week. Going on national television and calling your coach a narcoleptic, unhealthy, lazy person who doesn't even know the franchise he works for is insane. So, this is a moment that will ultimately rally the locker room, or cause them to completely fall apart. Pick which side you'd like. The Steelers have also won and covered in six straight home games. This seems like an appropriate time for that streak to end   …  Prediction: Broncos 20, Steelers 13
Dubin (Broncos -3.5): After the disaster that hit the Steelers this week, I just can't see them keeping the game close against the Broncos. No, I don't think they'll get the backup quarterback bounce from Mason Rudolph. I don't trust the Broncos as far as Bo Nix or I can throw them, but given the state the Steelers' locker room has to be in right now, I think you have to roll with Denver to cover this one with relative ease.  … Prediction: Broncos 24, Steelers 10Baltimore Ravens at Houston Texans (-7)Dajani (Ravens +7): I have the Houston Texans winning this game, but seven points seems a bit high. C.J. Stroud is playing some great football, but his production has been overshadowed by a defense that has fallen from No. 2 in points allowed per game in 2025, to 17th this year. The Texans are 1-8 against the spread in their last nine home games following an ATS win. I'll take Baltimore to keep it close… Prediction: Texans 24, Ravens 18Dubin (Ravens +7): The Ravens have now lost six straight, but they've lost the two games in the Jacoby Brissett era by a combined five points despite turning the ball over six times in those contests. If they can just limit the giveaways, I think they might even be able to pull off an upset against a Houston team that hasn't exactly lit the world on fire this year. Either way, I think they can keep it close by throwing on a surprisingly vulnerable Texans pass defense.  … Prediction: Texans 24, Ravens 20
Seattle Seahawks at San Francisco 49ers (-3)Dajani (49ers -3): Sam Darnold is expected to return this week, and he's accounted for 10 touchdowns compared to nine interceptions in seven starts this season. If you throw out the season opener that Drew Lock finished and won, Darnold is 2-4 as a starter this season.Believe it or not, San Francisco is 0-9 against the spread in its last nine home divisional games. With the number at a field goal, the 49ers have a good chance to end that streak this week. What they did to the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City last Sunday night was shocking. The 49ers should be headlining everyone's NFL power rankings if they weren't already. Their 0.19 EPA per play is the best mark since the 2018 Chiefs, and they have the best offensive success rate (54.8%) by any team in a season since at least 2000 …  Prediction: 49ers 24, Seahawks 20Dubin (49ers -3): I reserve the right to flip this prediction to Seattle if Brock Purdy is out with his ankle injury, but if he's in, I just think that this San Francisco offense is a buzzsaw that can't really be stopped — even by the Dark Side defense. Remember, they dropped 32 points on Seattle the last time out. And they've scored 35 or more in each of their three games since returning from the bye. I don't think they can be stopped when everyone is healthy.  … Prediction: 49ers 30, Seahawks 23
Las Vegas Raiders at Cleveland Browns (-4.5) (SNF)Dajani (Raiders +4.5): Maybe part of me is rooting for Fernando Mendoza in his first primetime start? Last week against the Broncos, he threw for 267 yards, three touchdowns and an interception. It was a solid performance, even though the rookie was sacked five times. The Raiders certainly have their weaknesses. They are on pace to become the first team since the 2022 Texans to finish bottom two in both rushing yards per game and opponent rushing yards per game, but this 6-4 Cleveland Browns team hasn't won a game by five-plus points since LAST YEAR. That gives me some optimism Vegas can cover  …  Prediction: Browns 24, Raiders 20Dubin (Raiders +4.5): I will continue to stand on the idea that this Browns team is not good. Every one of Cleveland's wins has required a game-winning drive in the final minutes of the fourth quarter. The Browns have been out-gained in seven of their 10 games and are somehow 6-4. That is not remotely sustainable. I think the Raiders pull off the upset behind Fernando Mendoza and a returning Brock Bowers. … Prediction: Raiders 21, Browns 17Carolina Panthers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-3) (MNF)Dajani (Panthers +3): I'm going to take the points with the Panthers because they are playing on the road. If you were unaware, Carolina is 3-2 away from Charlotte, and has a +8 turnover differential. The Panthers have a -4 turnover differential at home, and allow 37.4 points per game at Bank of America Stadium! For whatever reason, the Panthers are a better team on the road. 
It's true that the Tampa Bay Buccaneers throttled the Panthers in Week 7, 43-13, but I think Carolina splits the season series. The Buccaneers are 1-9 against the spread in their last 10 home games, and 0-7 against the spread in their last seven home primetime games. Baker Mayfield is a shocking 1-13 in primetime since 2021, so I'll back Bryce Young …  Prediction: Panthers 28, Buccaneers 27Dubin (Buccaneers -3): The last time these two teams played, the Bucs racked up 258 rushing yards. The Panthers' run defense then limited the Packers, Broncos and Saints over the next three games, but the Ravens hit them up for 157 yards last week. I don't see much reason to believe that the Bucs will be slowed on the ground, and I don't trust Carolina's offense to score enough to get the Bucs out of their run-heavy orientation.  … Prediction: Buccaneers 20, Panthers 16Chicago Bears (-1.5) at Detroit Lions (Thursday)Dajani (Bears -1.5): I can't remember being more excited for a Thanksgiving Day game, as the Bears and Lions are two of the best teams in the NFL. What I keep going back to is that the Bears are 6-0 while averaging 33.7 points in games where Caleb Williams starts and finishes. Then, factor in how much improved this Chicago defense looks with the addition of Jeffery Simmons. In Weeks 1-7, they ranked dead last in both yards per play (6.3) and yards per attempt (8.7). Over the last four weeks, the Bears now rank in the top 10 in both categories. Chicago has been swept by Detroit in each of the last two seasons. I think the Bears are done with losing to Dan Campbell …  Prediction: Bears 30, Lions 28
Dubin (Lions +1.5): These are two incredibly evenly-matched teams, but it seems like Detroit has more matchup advantages offensively against Chicago's improved defense than the Bears do against the Lions' own improved unit. With Detroit also getting the benefit of home-field advantage, we're rolling with the Lions to win a close one as a home underdog.  … Prediction: Lions 31, Bears 30Philadelphia Eagles at Dallas Cowboys (-8.5) (Thursday)Dajani (Cowboys -8.5): I don't think the Cowboys have exorcised all of their defensive demons just because they blew out the Tennessee Titans, but that win at home was just what this team needed. This is one of those cases where I think the Cowboys just simply out-score their opponent. This is still a rivalry, but the Eagles are 2-8 against the spread this season, which ranks second-worst in the NFL behind the Los Angeles Chargers, and are 0-5 against the spread in their last five divisional matchups. The Cowboys should get this cover in the fourth quarter. They have scored NINETY-ONE (91) points over the past two games! That's the most in a two-game span since 1971…  Prediction: Cowboys 33, Eagles 20Dubin (Eagles +8.5): I know they just beat the Titans by 21, but I don't like laying this many points with the Cowboys. Their defense is still too suspect and they are still too prone to games where they don't perform up to expectations for me to be comfortable with an 8.5-point spread. So even while I think they'll dent the scoreboard at home on Thanksgiving afternoon, I can't bring myself to predict that this will be a blowout. … Prediction: Cowboys 30, Eagles 24
Kansas City Chiefs at Buffalo Bills (-3) (Thursday)Dajani (Chiefs +3): The craziest part about this rivalry is that the Bills have won the last five regular-season meetings, while the Chiefs have won the last four playoff meetings! You should also know that the weather is supposed to be terrible on Thursday night, so this could come down to which team runs the ball better. James Cook has recorded nine straight games with 75 rushing yards and a touchdown. He and Josh Allen are the second duo to ever account for double-digit rushing touchdowns each through the first 10 games of a season. Meanwhile, on the other side, Emmett Johnson has rushed for 206 yards with 108 receiving yards and three touchdowns over the last two games in place of the injured Kenneth Walker III. I almost think a three-point spread in this matchup is pretty high. That's going to lead me to take the points even though Bills over Chiefs has been an auto-bet in the regular season recently… Prediction: Chiefs 17, Bills 16Dubin (Bills -3): I have basically the exact same analysis of this game as Dajani but come down on the opposite side of the bet because of the Bills' regular-season history against the Chiefs and the relative strength of their run game. I trust Josh Allen and James Cook to run the ball more than I do Emmett Johnson, even with how good Johnson has been over the last two weeks. Could Patrick Mahomes make this prediction look silly? Of course. But I think that'll prove more difficult in Thursday night's expected weather. … Prediction: Bills 21, Chiefs 17

title: Louisville's buzzer-beater ends St. John's comeback try: Five takeaways from craziest Players Era game to date - CBS Sports
description: LAS VEGAS — The craziest game of the first month of the college basketball season transpired when most of you who are reading this had l
body:
LAS VEGAS — The craziest game of the first month of the college basketball season transpired when most of you who are reading this had likely fallen asleep from eating way too much on Thanksgiving. To those who missed this ending in real time: I hope you learned your lesson. Never check out early on tournament hoops during turkey week. The best stuff often happens at the latest hours. Fortunately, yours truly was courtside at Michelob Ultra Arena on Thursday night to see No. 25 Louisville's theatric, buzzer-beating 93-90 win against No. 13 St. John's, handing Rick Pitino's team his first loss of the season. The win was all the more dramatic because it was Pitino's former school beating his current one in a game that was loaded with controversy, confusion, a huge comeback/collapse, some incredible performances and instantly viral moments. Adrian Wooley's 3-pointer from the left corner on a broken play got U of L its second straight win against a ranked opponent. Here's how the junior shooting guard kept the Cards alive for the Players Era 16 title at 8:29 p.m. local time on the Strip. 
Jackpot. "We played great defense, he made a lucky shot," Pitino said.  Cardinals coach Pat Kelsey called it a shot Woolely will "tell his grandkids about." Wooley said it felt like a movie. Typically, a good game happens and there's a column to write with a focused angle. That's not happening here. Way too much attached, so I'm going to try and touch on all the relevant angles tied to this one before Louisville plays No. 9 Tennessee on Friday (9 p.m. ET on ESPN) for the opportunity to win Saturday's Players Era 16 championship. 
 1. Wooley's trey saved Cards from an epic choke For most of the game, it looked like Louisville was going to give St. John's a loss that was on the level of the one Pitino's team took last season at UConn. Louisville scored 57 of its 93 points in the first half, the 57-39 difference marking the largest halftime deficit St. John's has been a part of since Pitino became coach. It was also the most points in a half Pitino's team has allowed since he's been with SJU.  Cards showed up ready to play; St. John's looked like it was recovering from a Vegas hangover. Then the full-court press started to work and a 20-3 St. John's run in the final four minutes got the game to toss-up status. The stifling defense combined with some Johnnies-on-the-spot buckets led to unexpected drama at a point when the game should've been decided. Ruben Prey's 3-pointer from the left wing with 20 seconds left cut it to a 90-88 Louisville lead.  
Louisville avoided overtime with the winning shot on the final possession after two St. John's free throws from Ian Jackson tied the game at 90. (Don't worry, I'm getting to that near-catastrophe in the next section.) Here's another look at Wooley's wily winner. 
The triple was just Wooley's 10th made 3-pointer of the season.  "Once I made the shot and I turned around, there was a kid standing right there and I felt like I was just staring into his soul," Wooley said when asked about the play. "It was like a movie." Louisville coach Pat Kelsey couldn't believe referees ruled Jackson Shelstead called a timeout UL didnt have. 
                                                                    Imagn Images
                                                             2. Officials dodge scandal, request for explanation Had St. John's found a way to come back from 24 points down to win this game, the Louisville collapse would've been overlooked because we would've had an officiating scandal that might have taken over the weekend in college sports. 
Official Tommy Johnson — according to what I saw and heard with my own eyes and ears, in addition to what ESPN's cameras caught and dozens of fans in the immediate vicinity of the play saw — incorrectly ruled that Louisville guard Jackson Shelstad called for a timeout with 13.7 seconds remaining and Louisville holding a 90-88 lead.  And wouldn't you know it, someone sitting courtside also caught the sequence on video. Watch and listen closely and you'll see that Shelstad doesn't call for timeout; this was just a gaffe by the official.  
The problem with calling a timeout is that Louisville didn't have any left, so that results in a technical foul and two free throws for the other team. Despite pleas from Louisville's bench (and plenty of fans in the arena), the officials didn't correct the mistake. Jackson made both foul shots, tying the game at 90. 
Then there was another twist: Louisville received the ball, by rule. That came as a surprise to Louisville's coaching staff. Kelsey said in the postgame press conference he thought St. John's would get the ball. Even Pitino indicated he thought SJU would get the ball.  Instead, Louisville got the ball with 13.7 to go on what wound up being the final possession of the game. Wooley's 3-pointer was as much of a ball-don't-lie vindication as you'll ever see.  The Athletic's CJ Moore approached the game officials afterward and requested a comment; the crew declined.  
That's not acceptable, not when a blown call is obvious and could have flipped a game result.  The call was so egregious, it prompted Kelsey to mime an attentive dog's pose. 
Refs owning up to mistakes and/or offering insight as to why calls do or don't get made in crucial end-game moments isn't an easy thing to do, but it should be the proper protocol. Had this been a conference or NCAA postseason game, we would've gotten more because of established procedures. Nonconference games allow officials to defiantly dodge media inquiries.  3. Pitino claims the matchup wasn't personalThe big story going into this game, of course, was Pitino facing Louisville for the first time since he was fired in October 2017.  
Pitino was asked about it in the postgame press conference, but given everything else that was involved in the game, this plot point wasn't nearly as prominent in the aftermath."I didn't have any, to be perfectly honest with you," Pitino said when asked about any strong emotions going into Thursday night. Now, if I was coaching in the Yum! Center, I think I'd have a lot. But it's just a terrific Louisville basketball team that we're trying to beat — no different than trying to beat Kentucky last year. ... I love the fans of Louisville, proud of what Pat Kelsey's doing with the team."I can't buy that Pitino wasn't in his feels over this game on some level. Playing Louisville in Las Vegas on Thanksgiving and with a crowd of maybe 3,500 on hand definitely made it easier because it wasn't in a hostile home/road environment.
But it's still Louisville. And Louisville represents the longest coaching tenure of his Hall of Fame career. He wanted to win this game, I'm sure, as much as any regular season opportunity he's had since getting back into college coaching in 2021. He had one hint at that desire.St. John's coach Rick Pitino was all smiles before facing Louisville coach Pat Kelsey. 
                                                                    Getty Images
                                                            "Things didn't go right for us in the first half but when we were down 12, I said we are going to win this game," Pitino said. "I couldn't be more proud of our basketball team in the way they fought back with incredible hustle, incredible desire to win."Kelsey, on the other hand, said it was an honor to face Pitino. You could hear the reverence in his voice. He said Pitino is maybe the greatest college coach of all time and referred to Pitino's patented full-court press as the best ever in the sport. Kelsey even apologized to Pitino's face for celebrating too hard at Wooley's game-winner, then having to stiffen up for the handshake line.
"It was an honor to coach against him," Kelsey said. 4. Game was a microcosm of courtroom implications  Oh, by the way: Seth Trimble had his best game as a college player on Thursday. He finished with a career-high 33 points off the bench and was the reason Louisville won, even with Wooley's incredible shot. That play, per Kelsey, was supposed to be for Trimble to get into the paint and have a shot close to the rim.So it was 33 points instead of 35."We got dominated by a great point guard tonight," Pitino said.Trimble, who is in his fifth season, is only playing because a judge has allowed him to do so against the wishes of the NCAA. Kelsey made huge headlines for his public display on the stand in defense of Trimble back in October. If that doesn't happen, Louisville likely isn't 2-0 at Players Era through Thursday and 6-1 overall. Trimble wasn't the only guy playing on Thursday night in this game who needed a friendly judge to see the floor, either.St. John's has multiple. Keyshawn Hall is one of them. He had 17 points and 10 rebounds for St. John's. Babacar Sane is another. He finished with 14 points for SJU.Given all that, I couldn't help but think that this game will prove be a microcosm of what we're going to see all season long. Teams will win big games, earn conference titles, good NCAA seeds and make the Final Four because of rulings made in their favor by judges.  Pitino took time to criticize the NCAA's end-of-June timing for changing the five-for-five rule. It's led to inconsistency across college sports."All that had to happen with all of this is come out with a ruling in November and December," Pitino said. "Why do it in the summer when all this money is involved? You knew that was going to happen, so it was mind-boggling that you could make such a traumatic mistake like that." 5. St. John's, Baylor screwed on schedulingScheduling two eight-team tournaments in two arenas with similar tip times means that adjusting for the winners' and losers' brackets will lead to a tight turnaround or two.But St. John's has to play Iowa State at 10 a.m. local time in the third-place game of the MUA (Michelob Ultra Arena) bracket on Friday. There will be people that read this story about the Louisville-SJU game after St. John's tips against the Cyclones. The turnaround is all of 13.5 hours, which is egregious. ESPN and Players Era organizers had to agree on the bracket format, of course, and TV's role in trying to maximize viewership with coinciding tournaments inevitably meant that a couple of teams were going to get squeezed on the third day of games. But asking any team to play on less than at least 16 hours worth of rest isn't justifiable. Pitino took issue with it, noting that Iowa State will prep with almost nine hours more rest, but also refused to allow for any excuses. "I don't think the tournament was very intelligent to have us turn around and play at 10 o'clock in the morning," Pitino said, then added, "if Iowa State beats us, it's not because we weren't ready to play. We will be ready."The same is true of Baylor, which lost just before 11 p.m. West Coast time on Thursday night against Gonzaga and will only get 13 hours before it faces TCU at noon local time Friday at T-Mobile Arena.  Both games are third-place games in their respective brackets. Why they have to be so early is strange. This isn't nearly as problematic as last year's 18-team Players Era field that couldn't be in a bracketed format, but it is one more tweak that needs to be addressed in 2027.

description: Plus, is Jahmyr Gibbs truly an MVP candidate?
body:
Plus, is Jahmyr Gibbs truly an MVP candidate?
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 27, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:07 am ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        You're probably on your second or third nap by now, right? No, we're not saying you're Mike McCarthy, nor are we saying you could coach the Pittsburgh Steelers (or Green Bay Packers, for that matter). We're merely pointing out that you've consumed enough tryptophan from the Thanksgiving turkey that you're probably a little lethargic. And if that means you dozed off during some of the NFL's Thanksgiving triple-header, that's alright. We're here to help you sift through what went down over the holiday slate and make you sound smart. Given that all three games were in individual windows and the entire nation was huddled around the table to watch them, there will be a lot of opinions that spew out of them. Some will be justified, while others you'll rightfully tilt your head, squint your eyebrows, and judge silently. We'll make you the former. Below, we'll go through some of the top storylines from each Thanksgiving game and determine if they're something to take seriously or if they're merely overreactions. The Bears are a shoo-in to win the NFC NorthOverreaction vs. reality: OverreactionWhen it comes to statement wins, you won't find many bigger than the Bears rolling into Ford Field and pulling off the 39-35 win over the Lions. Chicago scored the game-winning touchdown with just three seconds left in regulation and erased an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit. That victory puts the Bears at 9-2 on the season, and that has them atop the NFC North. 
Naturally, confidence is sky-high that Chicago will eventually secure the division title for the second straight year, and rightfully so. How can you not feel that way after such a marquee win? Should they be printing the hats and T-shirts, however? That's a different discussion entirely. While Chicago owns the inside track, the NFC North is far from being solidified. The Bears still have three division matchups on the docket over their final six games of the season. Outside of facing NFC North rivals, they'll also square off against the Jaguars and Bills. The only sure-fire victory is when they visit the Miami Dolphins in Week 14. With the margins still razor-thin, and the Bears currently 1-2 in the division, they are not on as solid ground as this latest win would suggest. Jahmyr Gibbs has entered the MVP conversationOverreaction vs. reality: OverreactionAt the end of the day, the MVP is a quarterback's award. You may not like it, but that's the reality. Gibbs has been otherworldly this season and just put together a historic performance on Thanksgiving. He logged 21 carries for 205 yards, three touchdowns, and five receptions for 47 yards. Those are the second-most rushing yards on Thanksgiving in NFL history, and Gibbs tied Barry Sanders (1997) for the most rushing touchdowns on Thanksgiving by a Lions player in franchise history. 
Gibbs has joined Eric Dickerson (1983) and Priest Holmes (2002) as the only players with at least 1,700 scrimmage yards and 18 total touchdowns in the first 11 games of a season in NFL history. 
Again, these numbers are bonkers and will almost certainly give Gibbs the inside track at the Offensive Player of the Year award. Those who Jim Nantz pointed out were chanting "MVP" at Ford Field on Thursday, however, will be disappointed. That'll go to Joe Burrow, Brock Purdy, or whichever quarterback endears himself to the NFL at large.He may deserve it, but the hardware Gibbs will be eyed for is OPOY and not MVP. 
Joe Milton should get a shot at being a full-time starterOverreaction vs. reality: RealityJalen Hurts is the obvious top option at quarterback once he returns to full health. We're not talking about Hurts' standing as QB1 in Philadelphia. However, Howie Roseman has once again pulled a rabbit out of his hat. He plucked Joe Milton III off Dallas' practice squad, and you can't deny that what we've seen out of Milton doesn't warrant a longer look as a full-time starter in the NFL. 
It might not be with the Eagles, but you can't deny the raw ability that Milton possesses. The arm talent is obvious, and he was able to hang in against Dallas in a high-profile Thanksgiving matchup on the road in just his third career start. The Eagles have done a fantastic job at parlaying assets into future draft capital. It's not out of the realm of possibility that they do the same with Milton -- who'll be a restricted free agent -- this offseason. For a team searching for a long-term starter at quarterback, why wouldn't you roll the dice on someone like Milton, who is 26 years old? He has far higher upside than Kirk Cousins, Geno Smith, Kyler Murray, and Daniel Jones, who'll also be free agents (albeit unrestricted) this offseason. 
Dallas is dead in the NFC East raceOverreaction vs. reality: RealityNail, meet coffin. The Cowboys can put their playoff hopes to bed, unofficially. After blowing a 21-point lead to the Eagles on Thanksgiving, Dallas drops to 5-7 on the season. For the moment, they're in third place in the NFC East, and the path to the playoffs feels nonexistent, even if mathematically there's still a chance. 
They already are on the wrong side of the tiebreaker with the Giants after losing the season opener. They still have a Week 17 matchup to fully determine if that tiebreaker will be a factor. If not, it'll come down to division record, where New York has the advantage through Week 12 (2-1-1 vs. 2-2). More dire for Dallas, the road ahead may make division and head-to-head tiebreakers moot. After falling to the Joe Milton-led Eagles, the Cowboys will now have to endure a three-game stretch of facing the Seahawks in Seattle, the Rams in Los Angeles (after the Week 14 bye), and then the Jacksonville Jaguars before they see the Giants. They'll, in all likelihood, be an underdog in all three of those games. If the oddsmakers are proved right, they're 5-10 before they kick off against the Giants. 
After Thursday's showing, it's hard to have any confidence that they'll persevere and make a legitimate push to a division title. Bill will secure the No. 1 seed in the AFCOverreaction vs. reality: OverreactionIt's not that Buffalo won't eventually land the No. 1 seed in the AFC, but it's hardly secure at this point even after a critical head-to-head win over Kansas City. The Bills are 10-1 on the season, which has them on the inside track for the first-round bye at the moment. However, the upcoming month does present some challenges. After heading up to New England to face a Drake Maye-less Patriots, Buffalo will face the Packers (road), Bears, and Broncos (road). That could result in some losses that open the door for some other contenders in the conference. Specifically, that Broncos matchup in Denver looms large on Christmas Day as Sean Payton's team is currently the closest to Buffalo for the top spot in the conference. Again, the Bills are in a great position to be the No. 1 seed, but we've got a long way to go before locking in first-round bye plans.

Our five bold calls for Week 12 include a career day for Quinshon Judkins and mounting pressure on the Seahawks to play Drew Lock

        When it comes to the holidays, it's best to expect the unexpected. Rarely do things go smoothly when everyone convenes for Thanksgiving, so it's the right idea to lie back and simply roll with the punches as they come in. For instance, you have no idea what that weird uncle will say at the dinner table, nor can you guarantee the turkey won't be overcooked. It's bound to go off the rails in some capacity, but the one constant that you can lean on is that there will be football to help distract you from the madness, including the dog running outside with one of the turkey legs. That said, even the NFL is unpredictable, so it's up to us to try and see the forest through the trees and anticipate what could be on the horizon. Below, we're going to highlight a handful of storylines/individual performances from Week 12 that may surprise some people, but not us. All NFL odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook. Colston Loveland feasts on Thanksgiving
It was a modest day at the office for the entire Bears offense in Week 11, but they edged out a 21-13 win over the Saints. For his part, Colston Loveland was targeted just three times. The tight end hauled in all three passes for 29 yards, but did have a thunderous touchdown in the second quarter. That score should serve as the appetizer for a possible eye-popping performance from the Bears star pass catcher in Chicago's upcoming Thanksgiving matchup with the Detroit Lions. This is the first of two matchups between these NFC North rivals this season, and first place in the division is hanging in the balance during this holiday contest. The Bears are a slight road favorite, and if they want to prove the oddsmakers right, featuring Loveland would go a long way in that endeavor. 
In Week 18 of last season (the last time Loveland played the Lions), the then rookie delivered arguably the best game of his career. He caught 10 of his 13 targets for 91 yards and a touchdown. Those receptions are still his career high. This season, the Lions have been extremely susceptible to tight ends, allowing the most receiving yards (740) and receiving touchdowns (11) to the position in the NFL. They're also giving up the third-most receptions (68) to the position group this season.  This is a tasty matchup that Ben Johnson and company should look to exploit to come out of Thanksgiving thankful for their ninth win of the season. Gambling angle to note: Colston Loveland's receiving yards prop for Week 12 is 54.5 (-109 to the Over). Loveland is +145 to score a touchdown. 
Rams sneak into playoff pictureThe vibes surrounding the Rams have been off ever since they kicked off their season opener in Australia. A season marred by injury has seen this once-dubbed "superteam" enter its bye last week at 6-4, on the outside looking in on the playoff picture as the No. 9 seed. As they emerge from the break, however, there is an opportunity in front of them to climb back into the playoff picture, but they'll need a little help. First and foremost, they'll need to take care of business during the NFL's first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game where they host the Packers. Green Bay is currently clinging to the No. 7 seed in the NFL at 6-4 on the season. A mere win over the Packers on Wednesday would temporarily vault L.A. into the No. 7 seed. However, if they want to hold onto it coming out of Week 12 entirely, they'll need to hold their nose and root for the San Francisco 49ers to defeat the Seattle Seahawks at home. That won't be a small feat as Seattle is coming off of its bye and the Niners are coming off an international game in Mexico City. That said, if San Francisco can fend off the defending champions, that'd create the necessary breathing room for the Rams to hold onto their spot in the playoff picture. If the Seahawks win, they'd draw even at 7-4 and retain the tiebreaker thanks to their superior divisional record. It's not an impossible needle to thread, but the Rams will need to get some help over the holiday weekend. 
Gambling angle to note: The Rams are -104 to make the playoffs. A Rams-49ers moneyline parlay pays out +159. Drew Lock takeover reaches fever pitch
A QB controversy has been brewing in the Pacific Northwest, specifically between Sam Darnold and Drew Lock. That talk about a QB controversy has been almost exclusively external, however, as the Seahawks have noted that Darnold -- who has missed the previous two games with rib and quad injuries -- will resume his role as QB1 when healthy. Head coach Mike Macdonald also noted that the team is optimistic that Darnold's return under center will come this week as they emerge from their bye and take on the San Francisco 49ers. Darnold has been sidelined for essentially four games so far (injured himself on the opening drive of the season opener), so we've seen what the offense looks like with Drew Lock at the helm. He's led Seattle to four wins (3-0 as the starter), while completing 73.1% of his passes and a 125.6 passer rating. By the numbers, Lock has outplayed Darnold from what we've seen so far in 2026, thus bringing up the question of whether or not to keep Lock as the starter. 
Seahawks QBs in 2026Sam DarnoldDrew LockW-L3-43-0Completion percentage60%73%Yards per attempt7.09.0TD-INT10-97-0Passer rating79.5125.6Again, Darnold will be the guy whenever he's ready to return, so there is no real controversy yet. However, if/when he returns this week, he might be set up for failure, as the 49ers are playing as well as any team in the NFL right now.If Darnold struggles and the Seahawks lose to the Niners to drop them to 6-5, that chatter to slot in Lock as QB1 will likely reach a fever pitch, particularly with the division and wild card races starting to slip away from them. Steelers fall out of the playoff pictureI flagged this in my Cover 32 column for Week 11, but it's worth highlighting yet again. The Pittsburgh Steelers are dangerously close to seeing their season fall out from under them. They were 6-2 entering Week 9, and upon their return to the field, have looked nothing like the club that appeared destined to make the playoffs amid Aaron Rodgers' final season. Pittsburgh has dropped two straight games over the past two weeks, which now has them starting to fall down the wild card standings. At 6-4, they're clinging to the No. 7 seed in the conference, which makes Friday's matchup at home against the Denver Broncos as close to a must-win as you'll find in Week 12. The Broncos are a 3-point road favorite in this game, so the oddsmakers are projecting Pittsburgh to fall to 6-5. If they do, they run dangerously close to falling out of the playoff picture entirely. Temporarily, that'd happen if the New England Patriots go to Los Angeles and beat the Los Angeles Chargers. New England would draw even at 6-5 with Pittsburgh but they own the head-to-head tiebreaker thanks to a Week 2 win. Of course, the Patriots will be without Drake Maye (fractured fibula), but things might be evened out on the QB front as Justin Herbert is currently in concussion protocol coming out of Week 11. That possibly sets up a Tommy DeVito vs. DJ Uiagalelei matchup that is a true coin flip. While the Patriots could oust them from a playoff spot for this weekend, the bigger long-term concern is the Houston Texans. They are hosting the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday and are 6.5-point favorites. The double whammy for Pittsburgh would be for them to lose on Friday, see the Patriots beat the Chargers to shoot them down to the No. 8 seed, and then the Texans beat the Ravens to push them to 5-6. That's set up a Week 13 matchup between Pittsburgh and Houston that could very well be the nail in the coffin for their season if they don't turn things around. Gambling angle to note: A Texans, Patriots, Broncos moneyline parlay is +329. Quinshon Judkins rushes for a career-high 
It hasn't been the sophomore surge that folks hoped to see from Judkins this season, as the Browns back has struggled to be consistent. His 3.4 yards per carry average is a tick lower than his 3.6 yards per carry over his rookie season and is averaging just 47 rushing yards per game (59.1 yards per game in 14 games as a rookie in 2025). However, Cleveland's "Sunday Night Football" matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders set Judkins up with a true bounce-back opportunity. The Raiders' run defense has been horrid so far in 2026. Coming into Week 12, Las Vegas is giving up the most rushing yards to running backs in the NFL this season (130.5 yards per game). Their 13 rushing touchdowns allowed are tied for the second-most in the league. The Raiders defense is coming off of a Week 11 loss to the Broncos, where rookie back Jonah Coleman steamrolled them for 111 yards on the ground and three rushing touchdowns. As he enjoyed his bye week, Judkins was probably licking his chops seeing Coleman post those numbers, knowing full well that he'll get to face them this coming week. Judkins, a 2025 second-round pick, has rushed for at least 100 yards just once in his young career. Well, it wouldn't shock us if he not only notched his second-career game with 100 yards on the ground, but surpassed his 110-yard rushing game from Week 5 last season for a new career-best mark. The Raiders have allowed a 100-yard rusher three times this season already.

With both rivals out of the playoff picture, bragging rights and Jeremiah Smith's Heisman campaign take center stage

        With both No. 21 Ohio State and Michigan eliminated from the Big Ten title and College Football Playoff pictures, Saturday's showdown between the heated rivals will be distilled to its purest form. In no way, shape or form is it about what comes next.While both teams are bowl-eligible, the 122nd meeting between the border foes carries no significant postseason implications. It's simply about bragging rights in college football's most heated and historic series. The 2026 season is going down as a disappointment for both the Wolverines (6-5, 3-5 Big Ten) and Buckeyes (7-4, 5-3). But any season that includes a win over the other can't be written off as a total failure. That's how much The Game means. The winner will head into bowl/portal season with a sense of satisfaction while the loser will be left to grapple with another gutting defeat from a season full of them.When Michigan and Ohio State play, records get thrown out the window, and we're reminded of what makes this sport special. The playoff and the portal are looming, but for a few hours on Saturday at Ohio Stadium, they won't be at the forefront of anyone's mind. Against that backdrop, let's dive into the details as Michigan and Ohio State prepare for their annual showdown.
  Ohio State vs. Michigan: Need to know  Michigan's coaching uncertainty: First-year coach Kyle Whittingham was always viewed as something of a stopgap hire after the Sherrone Moore era went up in flames following the 2025 season. The potential brevity of his tenure is now in clear focus amid a dismal 2026 campaign. Michigan just botched an athletic director hire, and there has been no official announcement on Whittingham's future. But it's fair to wonder if this is the end. The 67-year old former Utah coach has done nothing to inspire confidence that he is the answer moving forward for one of college football's most historic brands. It doesn't help Whittingham's case that Utah appears to have improved following his departure from that program.Redemption for the defense: If ever there was a spot for the maligned Ohio State defense to secure some redemption for its recent shortcomings, this is it. Michigan ranks No. 132 out of 138 teams in total offense. Among Power Four schools, only Michigan State averages fewer yards per game than the Wolverines, who are producing just 296 yards per contest. Things haven't improved much in the two weeks since Michigan fired offensive coordinator Jason Beck. Even after transitioning back to Bryce Underwood as their starting quarterback, the Wolverines have remained anemic through the air.Jeremiah Smith's Heisman campaign: Ohio State star receiver Jeremiah Smith remains a heavy betting favorite to win the Heisman Trophy (-400 at DraftKings). Even after a mid-October injury to quarterback Julian Sayin, the Buckeyes have still found ways to get the football into Smith's hands. Smith has reeled in 34 catches for 498 yards and five touchdowns over Ohio State's last four games. At this point, the only real threat to Smith's candidacy is if someone like Utah quarterback Devon Dampier (+500) or Miami quarterback Darian Mensah (+1550) turns in a legendary performance during their conference championship game. Since Smith won't be playing in a conference title game, this is his last chance to make an impression in his quest to become the first Ohio State receiver to win the Heisman.
Where to watch Ohio State vs. Michigan live  Date: Saturday, November 25 | Time: 12 p.m. ET  Location: Ohio Stadium -- Columbus, Ohio  TV: Fox | Live stream: Fubo (try free)  Ohio State vs. Michigan prediction, picks  While Michigan's offense is among the worst in college football, the Wolverines can play some defense. Only two teams have surpassed 300 yards of offense against Michigan this season. It's no certainty that an Ohio State offense operating with backup quarterback Luke Fahey will be able to move the football. If Michigan is able to run the football against an Ohio State defense that hasn't been at its best recently, it can run some clock and keep the football out of the Buckeyes' hands. Mix it all up, and you get a low-scoring, grimy rivalry game. Ohio State has the game's top playmaker in Jeremiah Smith, and he'll make a game-changing play at some point to help the Buckeyes win. But the Wolverines have enough defensive strength to keep it close. Pick: Michigan +10.5
